recipes.name: Greek Style Beef Stew
ingredients_raw: 1 (28 ounce) can whole plum tomatoes, undrained and quartered
2 potatoes, peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a 5-quart pressure cooker over medium-high heat. Add half the beef; cook and stir until well browned on all sides. Remove beef with a slotted spoon and set aside. Brown the remaining meat and set aside.

Place chopped onion in the pressure cooker; cook and stir for 1 minute. Add the garlic and stir for an additional minute. Pour in the red wine, red wine vinegar, and beef broth; stir in the tomato paste and mix well.
Grind or crush rosemary, oregano, and peppercorns in a mortar and pestle or spice grinder. Add crushed spices to the cooker with bay leaves, cumin, cinnamon, cloves, black pepper, and brown sugar.

Pour in tomatoes and their juice; rinse the can with 1/2 cup water and add the water to the cooker. Stir in potatoes and carrots. Return the browned meat to the pressure cooker. A 5-quart pot should be about half full and a little soupy; the potato will dissolve a bit and thicken it after cooking. Cover the pot and seal the lid.

Bring the pot up to high pressure over high heat. Reduce the heat to low, maintaining full pressure, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let the pressure reduce naturally. Taste the stew and add salt, if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Greek Style Beef Stew
raw_recipe.description: This Greek-style beef stew is filled with potatoes, carrots, onions, tomatoes, and spices. A little red wine and wine vinegar adds additional depth of flavor.

review.reviewBody: It's getting cold, stew weather! I guess the double secret step for this is to grind the bay leaves, picking out the main stems, couple peppercorns or pinch of coarse salt helps the grinding along.
Great soup, really hits the spot, had it with different kinds of bread, grilled and olive oil dip.

This was great! I've been looking for an alternative to traditional beef/venison flavours and this fits the bill. I didn't have any rosemary but it didn't taste like it was lacking anything without it. We had it with home-made bread and hubby and I really enjoyed it. Thanks for sharing.

Made this using black wildebeest, left out the cumin add I didn't have, added corn and peas, it came out devine.. you could taste the wildebeest with the flavors coming out properly and not ruining the meat itself.. I'm doing this again with winter coming.. lovely
Very flavorful. I followed slow cooker directions and it came out great.
This is a really good stew, with all the flavors of the spices. I did change it because it was a little bitter. I added a 1/3 cup of Heinz ketchup, and another tablespoon of brown sugar.
Good twist to the traditional beef stew. Added jalapeños for extra zing
I wasn't sure what to make of the cumin and the cinnamon...they changed the flavor that enough with the bay leaf it was hit or miss with my crowd.
v. good, add masala or pepper for more zing
